name: OH-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Michael Rulli running for re-election
Huge fundraising gap: Rulli raised $1.1M vs. Kirtley's ~$1K
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Rulli's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage leave the Democrat with no visible path; markets agree at roughly 95% Republican. No polls or expert ratings suggest movement, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any sign of Democratic outside spending or polling showing a competitive race would warrant revisiting, but none exists now.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 6th District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about R+17. First-term incumbent Michael Rulli is running for re-election after winning the seat in a 2024 special election. His Democratic challenger, Elizabeth Kirtley, has raised barely over a thousand dollars, while Rulli has brought in more than $1.1 million, giving him an overwhelming resource advantage.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets put Republican chances around 95%. With no evidence of a competitive environment, the race is rated Safe Republican, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of polling.
